source.text: לְכוּ֙ וְנָשׁ֣וּבָה אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י ה֥וּא טָרָ֖ף וְיִרְפָּאֵ֑נוּ יַ֖ךְ וְיַחְבְּשֵֽׁנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Come and let us return to Yahweh, for he has torn, and he will heal us; he has struck, and he will bind us up.

en.L: "Come, and let us return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has torn, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will heal us; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has struck, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bind us up.
en.B: "Come, let us return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q It is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who has torn us, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will heal us; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has struck us down, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bandage our wounds.
en.R: "Come, let us go back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q He has torn us apart, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make us well. \q He has hurt us, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bandage our wounds.

es.L: «Vengan y volvamos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha desgarrado, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos sanará; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha herido, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos vendará.
es.B: «Vengan, volvamos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. \q Es {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quien nos ha desgarrado, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos sanará; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos ha herido, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos vendará las heridas.
es.R: «Vengan, volvamos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. \q Nos ha despedazado, pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos sanará. \q Nos ha herido, pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos vendará las heridas.

ko.L: "자, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로 돌아가자. \q 그분께서 찢으셨으나 그분께서 우리를 고쳐 주시고, \q 그분께서 치셨으나 그분께서 우리를 싸매 주실 것이다.
ko.B: "자, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로 돌아가자. \q 우리를 찢으신 분이 그분이시니, 그분께서 우리를 낫게 하실 것이다. \q 우리를 치신 분이 그분이시니, 그분께서 우리 상처를 싸매 주실 것이다.
ko.R: "자, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 돌아가자. \q 그분께서 우리를 찢으셨지만, 우리를 다시 낫게 하실 것이다. \q 그분께서 우리를 아프게 하셨지만, 우리 상처를 싸매 주실 것이다.

fr.L: « Venez, et revenons {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ; \q car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a déchiré, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous guérira ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a frappé, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous pansera.
fr.B: « Venez, revenons {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. \q C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui nous a déchirés, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous guérira ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a frappés, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pansera nos blessures.
fr.R: « Venez, revenons {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. \q Il nous a mis en pièces, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous guérira. \q Il nous a blessés, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soignera nos blessures.

decisions.choice: the people speak: verses 1-3 are their words, answered by the LORD in verses 4-6
alternatives: the prophet's own call to the people, not quoted speech
decisions.reason: The speakers say "us" and speak of the LORD as "he", so these are the words of the people, not of God. The LORD has just said that he will go away until they seek him in their distress (5:15), and here they are heard resolving to do so. The poem does not say whether they mean it. The LORD's answer in verse 4, that their love vanishes like the morning mist, shows that their turning was shallow. Some read the verses as the prophet calling the people to return; the words would be the same, but they are not marked as speech. They are set in quotation marks here as words quoted inside the oracle.

decisions.choice: he has torn ... he has struck: the LORD himself dealt the blows of 5:12-14
decisions.reason: In 5:14 the LORD says that he will be like a lion to Ephraim and Judah and will tear them and go away. The people now admit that the wound came from him, so only he can heal it. They had gone to Assyria for healing and found none (5:13). The same pairing of wounding and healing is in Deuteronomy 32:39: "I wound and I heal".

decisions.choice: It is he who has torn us (B); torn us to pieces (R); bandage our wounds (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "he" before the verb for emphasis, which Balanced gives as "It is he who". Balanced and Readable add "us", which the Hebrew leaves implied, and say "bandage our wounds" for "bind up", the dressing of a wound.

decisions.choice: the people's words in « » from 6:1 to 6:3; "Vengan" with no plural_you span
decisions.reason: Verses 1-3 are the people's own words, so they take quotation marks, as the English does. "Vengan" is the people urging one another, "let us" rather than "you", so it is not set as a plural_you span; Spain's "Venid" would also serve.

decisions.choice: The people's words (6:1–3) are in the plain style among themselves, with -시- and "그분" for God
decisions.reason: They speak to one another about God, not to him, so they use the narrative style with the honorific, as the Psalms do when the speaker talks about God.

decisions.choice: the people's words (verses 1-3) stand in « », opened here and closed at the end of verse 3
decisions.reason: As the English: the meaning decision says the people speak and the LORD answers in verse 4, and speech quoted inside the oracle takes French quotation marks.

source.text: יְחַיֵּ֖נוּ מִיֹּמָ֑יִם בַּיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י יְקִמֵ֖נוּ וְנִחְיֶ֥ה לְפָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: He will revive us after two days; on the day the third he will raise us up, and we will live before him.

en.L: He will revive us after two days; \q on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will raise us up, \q so that we live before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: After two days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring us back to life; \q on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will raise us up, \q so that we may live in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.
en.R: After two days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give us new life. \q On the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will raise us up. \q Then we will live in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.

es.L: Nos dará vida después de dos días; \q al tercer día nos levantará, \q y viviremos delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Después de dos días nos devolverá la vida; \q al tercer día nos levantará, \q para que vivamos en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} presencia.
es.R: Después de dos días nos dará nueva vida. \q Al tercer día nos levantará. \q Entonces viviremos en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} presencia.

ko.L: 이틀 뒤에 그분께서 우리를 살리시고, \q 셋째 날에 우리를 일으키실 것이니, \q 우리가 그분 앞에서 살 것이다.
ko.B: 이틀이 지나면 그분께서 우리를 다시 살리시고, \q 셋째 날에는 우리를 일으켜 세우실 것이다. \q 그러면 우리가 그분 앞에서 살게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 이틀 뒤에 그분께서 우리에게 새 생명을 주실 것이다. \q 셋째 날에 그분께서 우리를 일으켜 세우실 것이다. \q 그러면 우리는 그분 앞에서 살 것이다.

fr.L: Il nous fera revivre après deux jours ; \q le troisième jour {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous relèvera, \q et nous vivrons devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Après deux jours, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous rendra la vie ; \q le troisième jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous relèvera, \q et nous vivrons en {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} présence.
fr.R: Après deux jours, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous donnera une vie nouvelle. \q Le troisième jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous relèvera. \q Alors nous vivrons en {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} présence.

decisions.choice: after two days ... on the third day: soon, within a short time
decisions.reason: Hebrew poetry often names a number and then the next one up ("for three ... and for four", Amos 1:3; Proverbs 30:15-18). Here the pattern says that recovery will come quickly and surely, as a wound or a fever passes within days. It does not set out a timetable.

decisions.choice: revive us ... raise us up: restore us to life and health
alternatives: the raising of individual dead people
decisions.reason: The first verb means to make alive or keep alive, the second to make stand up. After verse 1 the picture is of the wounded nation getting up from its sickbed, healed. The same verbs are used of bringing the dead back to life (2 Kings 8:5; Isaiah 26:19), so the people may be speaking of themselves as all but dead, as Ezekiel 37 pictures Israel as dry bones. The verse speaks of the people as a whole ("us"), not of one person.

decisions.choice: on the third day: translated as Hosea's words about the people's recovery
decisions.reason: Paul writes that Christ "was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures" (1 Corinthians 15:4; compare Luke 24:46). He does not name a passage, and from early times many Christian readers have heard Hosea 6:2 in his words. Jewish tradition also read the verse of the raising of the dead: the Aramaic Targum speaks of the day of the resurrection of the dead. In Hosea the speakers are the people of Israel and the subject is their quick recovery from the LORD's blows, and they are about to be told that their love does not last (verse 4). The wording here says what Hosea says and is not shaped to any later reading; readers who see a fuller meaning in Christ's resurrection find it in the same words.

decisions.choice: on the third day, at every level; bring us back to life (B), give us new life (R)
decisions.reason: "On the third day" stays word for word at every level, because the pattern of the numbers is the point of the line (m1) and readers will recognize it (m3). Balanced and Readable say "bring us back to life" and "give us new life" for "revive", and "in his presence" for "before him".

decisions.choice: "al tercer día" at every level
decisions.reason: As the English, the phrase is kept at every level; it is translated as Hosea's words about the people's recovery, as the meaning decision says.

source.text: וְנֵדְעָ֣ה נִרְדְּפָ֗ה לָדַ֨עַת֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה כְּשַׁ֖חַר נָכ֣וֹן מֽוֹצָא֑וֹ וְיָב֤וֹא כַגֶּ֨שֶׁם֙ לָ֔נוּ כְּמַלְק֖וֹשׁ י֥וֹרֶה אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And let us know, let us press on to know Yahweh; like dawn is sure his going forth, and he will come like the rain to us, like spring rain [that] waters [the] earth.

en.L: Let us know; let us press on to know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} going out is as sure as the dawn, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come like the rain to us, \q like the spring rain watering the earth."
en.B: Let us know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; let us press on to know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q His coming is as certain as the sunrise; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come to us like the showers, \q like the spring rain that waters the land."
en.R: Let us get to know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Let us try hard to know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q He will surely come to us, as surely as the sun rises. \q He will come to us like rain, \q like the spring showers that water the ground."

es.L: Conozcamos, esforcémonos por conocer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} salida es segura como la aurora, \q y vendrá a nosotros como la lluvia, \q como la lluvia de primavera que riega la tierra».
es.B: Conozcamos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}; esforcémonos por conocerlo. \q Su venida es tan segura como la salida del sol; \q vendrá a nosotros como los aguaceros, \q como la lluvia de primavera que riega la tierra».
es.R: Conozcamos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Hagamos todo lo posible por conocerlo. \q Vendrá a nosotros tan seguro como sale el sol. \q Vendrá a nosotros como la lluvia, \q como los aguaceros de primavera que riegan el suelo».

ko.L: 우리가 알자. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 알기에 힘쓰자. \q 그분께서 나오시는 것은 새벽처럼 확실하니, \q 그분께서 비처럼 우리에게 오시고, \q 땅을 적시는 봄비처럼 [오실 것이다]."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 알자. 그분을 알기에 힘쓰자. \q 그분께서 오시는 것은 해 뜨는 것처럼 확실하다. \q 그분께서 소나기처럼 우리에게 오시고, \q 땅을 적시는 봄비처럼 오실 것이다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 알자. 그분을 알려고 힘껏 애쓰자. \q 아침마다 해가 뜨는 것처럼 그분께서도 꼭 우리에게 오실 것이다. \q 그분께서 비처럼 우리에게 오실 것이다. \q 땅을 적시는 봄비처럼 오실 것이다."

fr.L: Et connaissons, efforçons-nous de connaître {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; \q {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sortie est aussi sûre que l’aurore, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra à nous comme la pluie, \q comme la pluie de printemps qui arrose la terre. »
fr.B: Connaissons {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; efforçons-nous de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaître. \q Sa venue est aussi certaine que le lever du soleil ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra à nous comme les averses, \q comme la pluie de printemps qui arrose le pays. »
fr.R: Apprenons à connaître {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Faisons tout pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaître. \q Il viendra à nous, c’est aussi sûr que le lever du soleil. \q Il viendra à nous comme la pluie, \q comme les averses de printemps qui arrosent le sol. »

decisions.choice: to know the LORD: to be close to him and loyal to him, not only to know about him
decisions.reason: In Hosea, knowing God is the bond of a faithful relationship that shows itself in loyalty and obedience (2:22; 4:1, 6). The people say they want it; in verse 6 the LORD says that it is what he desires, and the rest of the chapter shows how far they are from it. The verb "press on" means to pursue or chase after something.

decisions.choice: his going out is as sure as the dawn: he will appear to help as surely as the sun rises
decisions.reason: The people picture the LORD coming out to help them as the sunrise, which never fails, and as the rain, which brings the land back to life. The LORD takes up their pictures in reply: their love is like the mist and dew that the morning sun burns off (verse 4), and his judgment goes out like the light (verse 5).

decisions.choice: like the spring rain that waters the earth
alternatives: like the spring rain and the autumn rain on the earth
decisions.reason: The second rain word means the late rain of spring, which ripens the grain before harvest. The word after it can be read as a verb, "that waters", or as the name of the early rain of autumn, which softens the ground for plowing (Deuteronomy 11:14; Joel 2:23 names both rains). Read the second way, the line is "like the spring rain and the autumn rain on the earth". The sense is the same: the LORD will come as surely as the rains that bring the harvest.

decisions.choice: his coming (B); He will surely come to us (R); the closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: "Going out" is the word for the rising of the sun; Balanced says "coming" because the next line says that he will come. Readable makes "sure as the dawn" a sentence of its own. The people's words end here, so the quotation mark opened in verse 1 closes.

source.text: מָ֤ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לְּךָ֙ אֶפְרַ֔יִם מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂה־לְּךָ֖ יְהוּדָ֑ה וְחַסְדְּכֶם֙ כַּֽעֲנַן־בֹּ֔קֶר וְכַטַּ֖ל מַשְׁכִּ֥ים הֹלֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: What shall I do to you, Ephraim? What shall I do to you, Judah? And your loyal love [is] like a cloud of morning, and like the dew early going away.

en.L: What shall I do with you, Ephraim? \q What shall I do with you, Judah? \q Your loyal love [is] like a morning cloud, \q and like the dew that goes away early.
en.B: What am I to do with you, Ephraim? \q What am I to do with you, Judah? \q Your loyal love is like the morning mist, \q like the dew that vanishes early in the day.
en.R: Ephraim, what am I going to do with you? \q Judah, what am I going to do with you? \q Your faithful love disappears like the morning mist, \q like the dew that is gone soon after sunrise.

es.L: ¿Qué haré contigo, Efraín? \q ¿Qué haré contigo, Judá? \q Su amor leal [es] como nube de la mañana, \q y como el rocío que temprano se va.
es.B: ¿Qué voy a hacer contigo, Efraín? \q ¿Qué voy a hacer contigo, Judá? \q Su amor fiel es como la niebla de la mañana, \q como el rocío que desaparece temprano.
es.R: Efraín, ¿qué voy a hacer contigo? \q Judá, ¿qué voy a hacer contigo? \q Su amor fiel desaparece como la niebla de la mañana, \q como el rocío que se va poco después de salir el sol.

ko.L: 에브라임아, 내가 너를 어떻게 하겠느냐? \q 유다야, 내가 너를 어떻게 하겠느냐? \q 너희의 한결같은 사랑은 아침 구름 같고, \q 일찍 사라지는 이슬 같다.
ko.B: 에브라임아, 내가 너를 어떻게 하면 좋겠느냐? \q 유다야, 내가 너를 어떻게 하면 좋겠느냐? \q 너희의 한결같은 사랑은 아침 안개 같고, \q 이른 아침에 사라지는 이슬 같다.
ko.R: 에브라임아, 내가 너를 어떻게 해야 하겠느냐? \q 유다야, 내가 너를 어떻게 해야 하겠느냐? \q 너희의 변함없는 사랑은 아침 안개처럼 사라지고, \q 해가 뜨면 곧 없어지는 이슬과 같다.

fr.L: Que te ferai-je, Éphraïm ? \q Que te ferai-je, Juda ? \q Votre amour loyal [est] comme un nuage du matin, \q et comme la rosée qui s’en va de bonne heure.
fr.B: Que vais-je faire de toi, Éphraïm ? \q Que vais-je faire de toi, Juda ? \q Votre amour fidèle est comme la brume du matin, \q comme la rosée qui disparaît tôt dans la journée.
fr.R: Éphraïm, que vais-je faire de toi ? \q Juda, que vais-je faire de toi ? \q Votre amour fidèle disparaît comme la brume du matin, \q comme la rosée qui s’en va peu après le lever du soleil.

decisions.choice: the LORD answers the people's words with a lament
decisions.reason: The speaker changes: "I" is now the LORD, answering verses 1-3. The questions are not a threat but the cry of someone who has tried everything, like a parent with a child who will not change (compare 11:8). Ephraim is the northern kingdom (see 4:17); Judah stands beside it in guilt, as in 5:10-14.

decisions.choice: your loyal love: the love and loyalty the people owed the LORD
decisions.reason: This is *hesed*, the faithful love that keeps a covenant bond. It is the very thing the LORD says he desires in verse 6, and its absence from the land is one of his charges against Israel in 4:1. The people's *hesed* is real enough for a moment, but it does not last.

decisions.choice: like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes away early
decisions.reason: In the dry summer of Israel, mist and dew form in the night and are gone soon after the sun rises. The people expected the LORD to come like the rain (verse 3); their own love is a mist that brings no rain. Hosea uses the same picture of the people themselves in 13:3.

decisions.choice: loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *hesed* in the prophets. It is kept the same here as in verse 6, so that the reader can see that the people's love fails in the very thing God asks for.

decisions.choice: "Su amor leal" (L); "Su amor fiel" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "your" is plural here, Ephraim and Judah together; Spanish "su" fits ustedes, and no plural_you span is needed because "su" with "amor" cannot be misread after the two names.

decisions.choice: "한결같은 사랑" (L, B), "변함없는 사랑" (R) for the people's *hesed* too
decisions.reason: The same word as God's *hesed* in 2:21 and 6:6, so the contrast between his love and theirs stays visible; Korean can say it without irony because the clause says how quickly it vanishes.

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֗ן חָצַ֨בְתִּי֙ בַּנְּבִיאִ֔ים הֲרַגְתִּ֖ים בְּאִמְרֵי־פִ֑י וּמִשְׁפָּטֶ֖יךָ א֥וֹר יֵצֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore I have hewn [them] by the prophets; I have killed them by [the] words of my mouth; and your judgments [are] light [that] goes forth.

en.L: Therefore I have hewn [them] by the prophets; \q I have killed them by the words of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth; \q and your judgments [are] light [that] goes forth.
en.B: That is why I have cut them down by the prophets; \q I have killed them with the words of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth, \q and the judgment on you goes out like the light.
en.R: That is why I have used the prophets to cut them down. \q I have struck them dead with the words I spoke. \q The judgment on you shines out as clearly as daylight.

es.L: Por eso [los] he cortado por medio de los profetas; \q los he matado con las palabras de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} boca; \q y tus juicios [son] luz [que] sale.
es.B: Por eso los he derribado por medio de los profetas; \q los he matado con las palabras de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} boca, \q y el juicio contra ti sale como la luz.
es.R: Por eso he usado a los profetas para derribarlos. \q Los he herido de muerte con las palabras que dije. \q El juicio contra ti brilla tan claro como la luz del día.

ko.L: 그러므로 내가 예언자들을 통해 [그들을] 찍어 냈고, \q 내 입의 말로 그들을 죽였다. \q 너에게 내린 심판은 빛처럼 나아간다.
ko.B: 그래서 내가 예언자들을 시켜 그들을 찍어 쓰러뜨리고, \q 내 입에서 나온 말로 그들을 죽였다. \q 너에게 내리는 심판은 빛처럼 퍼져 나간다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 예언자들을 시켜 그들을 쓰러뜨렸다. \q 내가 한 말로 그들을 죽였다. \q 너에게 내리는 심판은 대낮처럼 환히 드러난다.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi je [les] ai taillés par les prophètes ; \q je les ai tués par les paroles de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} bouche ; \q et tes jugements [sont] une lumière [qui] sort.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi je les ai abattus par les prophètes ; \q je les ai tués par les paroles de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} bouche, \q et le jugement contre toi sort comme la lumière.
fr.R: Voilà pourquoi je me suis servi des prophètes pour les abattre. \q Je les ai frappés à mort par les paroles que j’ai dites. \q Le jugement contre toi brille aussi clairement que la lumière du jour.

decisions.choice: hewn by the prophets, killed by the words of my mouth: the prophets' word brings about the judgment it announces
decisions.reason: "Hew" is the work of cutting stone or timber. The LORD's word through his prophets is pictured as an axe or a sword: what it announces comes to pass (Jeremiah 1:10; 23:29; 1 Kings 19:17). "Them" are the people of Ephraim and Judah of verse 4. "Therefore" ties this to verse 4: because their love keeps vanishing, the LORD has sent hard words.

decisions.choice: and your judgments are light that goes out: the judgment on you comes into the open like daylight
alternatives: and my judgment goes out like the light (dividing the letters differently, with the Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "and your judgments, light goes out". "Your" is best taken as the judgment passed on you, and the light as the open daylight in which it is seen (compare Zephaniah 3:5, "every morning he brings his justice to light"). The Greek translation and other ancient versions divide the same letters differently and read "and my judgment goes out like the light". That reading is smoother, and the sense is nearly the same. The translation follows the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: cut them down (B, R); goes out like the light (B); shines out as clearly as daylight (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "cut down" for "hew", which in English is used mostly of stone. They add "like" to make the picture of light plain; the Hebrew puts the judgment and the light side by side.

source.text: כִּ֛י חֶ֥סֶד חָפַ֖צְתִּי וְלֹא־זָ֑בַח וְדַ֥עַת אֱלֹהִ֖ים מֵעֹלֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: For loyal love I desire, and not sacrifice, and knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.

en.L: For I desire loyal love, and not sacrifice, \q and knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
en.B: For I want loyal love, not sacrifice, \q and knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
en.R: I want faithful love, not sacrifices. \q I want you to know God, more than I want you to bring burnt offerings.

es.L: Porque quiero amor leal y no sacrificio, \q y conocimiento de Dios más que holocaustos.
es.B: Lo que quiero es amor fiel, no sacrificios, \q y conocimiento de Dios más que holocaustos.
es.R: Quiero amor fiel, no sacrificios. \q Quiero que {{plural_you:conozcan|conozcáis}} a Dios, más que {{plural_you:me traigan|me traigáis}} holocaustos.

ko.L: 나는 한결같은 사랑을 원하고 제사를 [원하지] 않으며, \q 번제보다 하나님을 아는 지식을 [원한다].
ko.B: 나는 한결같은 사랑을 원하지 제사를 원하지 않는다. \q 번제보다 하나님을 아는 지식을 원한다.
ko.R: 나는 변함없는 사랑을 원하지 제물을 원하지 않는다. \q 너희가 번제물을 가져오는 것보다 하나님을 알기를 더 원한다.

fr.L: Car je désire l’amour loyal, et non le sacrifice, \q et la connaissance de Dieu plus que les holocaustes.
fr.B: Car c’est l’amour fidèle que je veux, et non le sacrifice, \q et la connaissance de Dieu plus que les holocaustes.
fr.R: Je veux l’amour fidèle, et non des sacrifices. \q Je veux que vous connaissiez Dieu, plus que je ne veux que vous apportiez des holocaustes.

decisions.choice: loyal love: steadfast, faithful love that keeps the covenant bond
decisions.reason: *Hesed* is the loyalty and kindness that people bound together owe each other: faithfulness to God, and faithfulness and mercy toward one another. It is the word that vanished like the dew in verse 4. It is wider than "mercy" or "kindness" alone, because it is love that stays loyal.

decisions.choice: not sacrifice ... more than burnt offerings: loyalty ranks above offerings
decisions.reason: Hebrew often says "A and not B" to mean "A rather than B", and the second line makes it plain: "more than burnt offerings". God is not banning sacrifice, which his own law commanded, but saying that offerings brought by people with no loyalty are worthless to him. The prophets and psalms say the same (1 Samuel 15:22; Psalm 51:18-19; Isaiah 1:11-17; Amos 5:21-24; Micah 6:6-8).

decisions.choice: knowledge of God: knowing God in a faithful relationship
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one of 4:1 and 4:6, and answers the people's "let us know the LORD" (verse 3). It is the knowing of a person, which shows in loyalty and obedience, not only knowing facts about God.

decisions.choice: Matthew 9:13 and 12:7 quote this verse in its Greek form, "I desire mercy, and not sacrifice"
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the first line twice: when he is criticized for eating with tax collectors and sinners (Matthew 9:13), and when his hungry disciples pick grain on the Sabbath (Matthew 12:7). Matthew gives the words in Greek, where the word for *hesed* is "mercy", and that is how Matthew is translated. Hosea's Hebrew word is wider: loyal love, toward God and toward others. Jesus applies the saying to showing mercy to people, which is part of what *hesed* means. Like Hosea, he ranks the one above the other.

decisions.choice: loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R); not "mercy"
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *hesed* in the prophets, the same as in verse 4. Many English Bibles have "mercy" here, the word of the Greek translation and of Matthew; that word is kept in Matthew, where it translates the Greek, but here the Hebrew is translated. Readable says "know God" for "knowledge of God", as the Hosea table sets, and repeats "I want" to show the ranking.

decisions.choice: "amor leal" (L); "amor fiel" (B, R), not "misericordia"
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: Hosea's Hebrew has hesed, so Spanish keeps the prophets' word. Matthew 9:13 and 12:7 quote the verse in its Greek form, which the Spanish Matthew gives as "misericordia".

decisions.choice: *hesed* "한결같은 사랑" (L, B), "변함없는 사랑" (R), not "자비"
decisions.reason: Matthew 9:13 and 12:7 quote this verse from the Greek (*eleos*), which the Korean New Testament renders "자비"; the Hebrew says *hesed*, the covenant love of 2:21 and 6:4, so Hosea keeps the settled word. The rest of the line keeps the Gospel's shape so the quotation can be recognised.

decisions.choice: "je veux ... et non le sacrifice" as the published Matthew 9:13, but "l'amour loyal" (L), "l'amour fidèle" (B, R) for hesed, not Matthew's "la miséricorde"
alternatives: "Je veux la miséricorde, et non le sacrifice"
decisions.reason: Matthew quotes the Greek, whose word means mercy; the Hebrew word is the covenant love the rest of Hosea speaks of, so French keeps Hosea's term and shares Matthew's other words so the quotation can still be seen.

source.text: וְהֵ֕מָּה כְּאָדָ֖ם עָבְר֣וּ בְרִ֑ית שָׁ֖ם בָּ֥גְדוּ בִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: But they like Adam have transgressed [the] covenant; there they have dealt faithlessly with me.

en.L: But they, \q like Adam, have transgressed [the] covenant; \q there they have dealt faithlessly with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: But like Adam they have broken the covenant; \q there they have betrayed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: But like Adam, they have broken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant. \q There they have been unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Pero ellos, \q como Adán, han transgredido el pacto; \q allí {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} han traicionado.
es.B: Pero ellos, como Adán, han quebrantado el pacto; \q allí {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} han traicionado.
es.R: Pero ellos, como Adán, han quebrantado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto. \q Allí {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} han sido infieles.

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 \q 아담처럼 언약을 어겼고, \q 거기에서 나를 배신했다.
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 아담처럼 언약을 깨뜨렸고, \q 거기에서 나를 배신했다.
ko.R: 그러나 그들은 아담처럼 내 언약을 깨뜨렸다. \q 거기에서 그들은 나에게 신실하지 않았다.

fr.L: Mais eux, \q comme Adam, ont transgressé [l’]alliance ; \q là, ils ont agi avec perfidie envers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Mais comme Adam, ils ont rompu l’alliance ; \q là, ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont trahi.
fr.R: Mais comme Adam, ils ont rompu {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} alliance. \q Là, ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont été infidèles.

decisions.choice: like Adam: the first man, who broke the command God gave him
alternatives: like human beings, they broke the covenant
at Adam they broke the covenant (a town, reading "at" for "like")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word can be a name or the ordinary word for a human being, and it can also be the name of a town, so the phrase has three possible senses. (1) Like Adam, the first man, who disobeyed God's command in the garden (Genesis 2:16-17; 3:6). Genesis does not call that command a covenant, but Hosea may describe it as one. (2) Like human beings: they broke the covenant as people always do (compare Psalm 82:7, "you will die like human beings"). (3) At Adam, the town by the Jordan where the waters stopped when Israel crossed into the land (Joshua 3:16). This reading fits the word "there" and the place names that follow (Gilead, Shechem), but it needs a one-letter change in the Hebrew, from "like" to "at". A translation has to choose one, and this one takes the first, which the Hebrew text supports as it stands.

decisions.choice: there: at a place the hearers knew, perhaps the places named in verses 8-9
decisions.reason: "There" points to a place, and the Hebrew does not say which one, unless "Adam" is read as a town (m1). It may point forward to Gilead and the road to Shechem, or back to the shrines of 4:15 and 5:1. The sense of the line is clear even so: the covenant was broken in real places where Israel lived and worshiped.

decisions.choice: transgressed the covenant ... dealt faithlessly: broke faith as a partner breaks a sworn bond
decisions.reason: "Transgress" means to cross over a line; the same phrase returns in 8:1, "they have transgressed my covenant". The second verb is used of a faithless husband or wife (Jeremiah 3:20; Malachi 2:14), which fits Hosea's picture of Israel as the LORD's unfaithful wife.

decisions.choice: broken the covenant (B); broken my covenant (R); betrayed (B); been unfaithful (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "broken" for "transgressed". Readable adds "my": the covenant is the LORD's, as 8:1 says. Literal keeps the order of the Hebrew, with "they" set apart before "like Adam".

decisions.choice: "han transgredido" (L); "han quebrantado" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Avar of a covenant is to cross over or break it; Literal keeps "transgredir" (kept apart from pasha only by context), Balanced and Readable say "quebrantar", as the English "broken".

source.text: גִּלְעָ֕ד קִרְיַ֖ת פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן עֲקֻבָּ֖ה מִדָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Gilead [is a] city of doers of wickedness, tracked with blood.

en.L: Gilead [is] a city of doers of wickedness, \q tracked with blood.
en.B: Gilead is a city of evildoers, \q marked with bloody footprints.
en.R: Gilead is a town full of people who do evil. \q Their bloody footprints are everywhere.

es.L: Galaad [es] ciudad de hacedores de maldad, \q marcada de sangre.
es.B: Galaad es una ciudad de malhechores, \q llena de huellas de sangre.
es.R: Galaad es un pueblo lleno de gente que hace el mal. \q Sus huellas de sangre están por todas partes.

ko.L: 길르앗은 악을 행하는 자들의 성읍이니, \q 피 묻은 발자국으로 덮였다.
ko.B: 길르앗은 악한 자들의 성읍이어서, \q 피 묻은 발자국이 가득하다.
ko.R: 길르앗은 악한 짓을 하는 사람들이 가득한 성읍이다. \q 가는 곳마다 피 묻은 발자국이 있다.

fr.L: Galaad [est] une ville de malfaiteurs, \q marquée de sang.
fr.B: Galaad est une ville de malfaiteurs, \q couverte d’empreintes de sang.
fr.R: Galaad est une ville pleine de gens qui font le mal. \q On y voit partout des traces de pas pleines de sang.

decisions.choice: Gilead: the land east of the Jordan, here spoken of as a city
alternatives: a region pictured as a city
decisions.reason: Gilead is usually the hill country east of the Jordan. Here it is called a city: perhaps a town of that name, perhaps Ramoth-gilead, one of the cities of refuge (Joshua 20:8), perhaps the region pictured as one town full of crime. In 2 Kings 15:25, fifty men of Gilead helped Pekah murder King Pekahiah in Samaria. Hosea may have such violence in mind, but he does not say so.

decisions.choice: tracked with blood: covered with bloody footprints
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for "heel" and is used rarely. Here it seems to mean marked with footprints, so the city is tracked with the footprints of people who have shed blood. A related word means "deceitful" (Jeremiah 17:9), and some read "treacherous with blood". Either way the city is full of violence.

decisions.choice: evildoers (B); people who do evil (R); bloody footprints
decisions.reason: "Doers of wickedness" is a phrase from the Psalms (Psalm 5:6; 6:9). Balanced says "evildoers"; Readable spells it out. Both make the footprints plain.

source.text: וּכְחַכֵּ֨י אִ֜ישׁ גְּדוּדִ֗ים חֶ֚בֶר כֹּֽהֲנִ֔ים דֶּ֖רֶךְ יְרַצְּחוּ־שֶׁ֑כְמָה כִּ֥י זִמָּ֖ה עָשֽׂוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And as lie in wait for a man raiders, a band of priests; [on the] road they murder toward Shechem; indeed, a shameful crime they have done.

en.L: And as raiders lie in wait for a man, so [is] a band of priests; \q on the road they murder toward Shechem; \q indeed, they have done a shameful crime.
en.B: Like bandits lying in wait for a victim, so is a gang of priests; \q they murder on the road to Shechem; \q what they have done is a vile crime.
en.R: The priests are like a gang of robbers waiting to attack someone. \q They murder people on the road to Shechem. \q They have done evil and shameful things.

es.L: Y como los salteadores que acechan a un hombre, [así es] la banda de sacerdotes; \q en el camino asesinan hacia Siquem; \q ciertamente han cometido una infamia.
es.B: Como bandidos que acechan a su víctima, así es la pandilla de sacerdotes; \q asesinan en el camino a Siquem; \q lo que han hecho es un crimen infame.
es.R: Los sacerdotes son como una banda de ladrones que espera para atacar a alguien. \q Asesinan a la gente en el camino a Siquem. \q Han hecho cosas malvadas y vergonzosas.

ko.L: 강도들이 사람을 숨어서 기다리듯 제사장 무리가 그러하다. \q 그들이 세겜으로 가는 길에서 살인한다. \q 참으로 그들이 부끄러운 범죄를 저질렀다.
ko.B: 강도들이 사람을 노리고 숨어 기다리듯 제사장 무리가 그렇게 한다. \q 그들은 세겜으로 가는 길에서 살인한다. \q 그들이 저지른 일은 추악한 범죄다.
ko.R: 제사장들은 사람을 덮치려고 숨어 기다리는 강도 떼와 같다. \q 그들은 세겜으로 가는 길에서 사람들을 죽인다. \q 그들은 악하고 부끄러운 짓을 저질렀다.

fr.L: Et comme des pillards guettent un homme, ainsi [fait] une bande de prêtres ; \q sur le chemin ils assassinent vers Sichem ; \q oui, ils ont commis une infamie.
fr.B: Comme des brigands qui guettent une victime, telle est la bande des prêtres ; \q ils assassinent sur la route de Sichem ; \q ce qu’ils ont fait est un crime infâme.
fr.R: Les prêtres sont comme une bande de voleurs qui attendent pour attaquer quelqu’un. \q Ils tuent des gens sur la route de Sichem. \q Ils ont fait des choses mauvaises et honteuses.

decisions.choice: as raiders lie in wait for a man, so does a band of priests
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of the first line is hard: the verb form is unusual, and the words run on with no clear link between them. The general sense is clear: the priests, who should teach the people God's ways (4:6), behave like a gang of highway robbers.

decisions.choice: on the road toward Shechem
decisions.reason: Shechem was an ancient place of covenant (Joshua 24:1, 25), a city of refuge and a town of the Levites (Joshua 20:7; 21:21). A city of refuge was a place where someone who had killed by accident could flee for safety. Murder on the road to such a city is all the more shameful. Who the victims were, perhaps travelers or pilgrims, the text does not say.

decisions.choice: a shameful crime: a planned, wicked act
decisions.reason: The word means a deliberate evil, often sexual sin (Leviticus 18:17; Judges 20:6), and also wicked schemes in general (Psalm 26:10). Here it sums up the priests' murders.

decisions.choice: a victim (B); someone, people (R); bandits, gang of robbers
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a man" in the general sense of anyone; Balanced and Readable say "a victim" and "someone". Readable names the victims "people", which the Hebrew implies.

source.text: בְּבֵית֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רָאִ֖יתִי שַׁעֲרֽוּרִיָּ֑ה שָׁ֚ם זְנ֣וּת לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם נִטְמָ֖א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing; there [is the] prostitution of Ephraim; Israel is defiled.

en.L: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing; \q Ephraim's prostitution [is] there; Israel is defiled.
en.B: In the house of Israel I have seen something horrible: \q Ephraim's prostitution is there, and Israel has become unclean.
en.R: I have seen something horrible in the nation of Israel. \q Ephraim has been unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and Israel has made itself unclean.

es.L: En la casa de Israel he visto una cosa horrible; \q allí [está] la prostitución de Efraín; Israel está contaminado.
es.B: En la casa de Israel he visto algo horrible: \q allí está la prostitución de Efraín, e Israel se ha vuelto impuro.
es.R: He visto algo horrible en la nación de Israel. \q Efraín {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha sido infiel, e Israel se ha hecho impuro.

ko.L: 이스라엘 집에서 내가 끔찍한 일을 보았다. \q 거기에 에브라임의 음행이 있고, 이스라엘이 더럽혀졌다.
ko.B: 나는 이스라엘 집에서 끔찍한 일을 보았다. \q 거기에서 에브라임이 음행했고, 이스라엘이 더러워졌다.
ko.R: 나는 이스라엘 나라에서 끔찍한 일을 보았다. \q 에브라임은 나에게 신실하지 않았고, 이스라엘은 스스로를 더럽혔다.

fr.L: Dans la maison d’Israël j’ai vu une chose horrible ; \q la prostitution d’Éphraïm [est] là ; Israël est souillé.
fr.B: Dans la maison d’Israël j’ai vu une chose horrible : \q là se trouve la prostitution d’Éphraïm, et Israël s’est rendu impur.
fr.R: J’ai vu une chose horrible dans la nation d’Israël. \q Éphraïm {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a été infidèle, et Israël s’est rendu impur.

decisions.choice: a horrible thing: something shocking and revolting
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning to shudder. Jeremiah uses related words for the horrible things done in Judah and by its prophets (Jeremiah 5:30; 18:13; 23:14). The Hebrew text's written and read forms of the word differ slightly in spelling, not in meaning.

decisions.choice: prostitution: unfaithfulness to the LORD in the worship of other gods
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb *zanah*, which Hosea uses throughout for Israel turning from the LORD to the Baals and other gods, pictured as a wife's unfaithfulness (1:2; 4:12-13). The worship at the shrines may also have included sexual rites (4:14), so the picture is not only a figure of speech.

decisions.choice: Israel is defiled: the same words as 5:3
decisions.reason: In 5:3 the LORD says: "Ephraim, you have prostituted yourself; Israel is defiled." Defiled means made unclean, unfit to come near God. The verse repeats the charge after the crimes of verses 8-9.

decisions.choice: the nation of Israel; been unfaithful to me; made itself unclean
decisions.reason: Readable says "nation" for "house", "been unfaithful" for the prostitution, as the Hosea table sets, and adds "to me", since it is the LORD who is betrayed. "Defiled" becomes "made itself unclean".

decisions.choice: "Israel está contaminado" (L); "Israel se ha vuelto impuro" (B); "Israel se ha hecho impuro" (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as 5:3 at each level, since the Hebrew repeats them.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘이 더럽혀졌다" (L), "이스라엘은 더러워졌다" (B), "이스라엘은 스스로를 더럽혔다" (R), as 5:3
decisions.reason: The book repeats the line of 5:3; Korean repeats its wording at each level so the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: a harvest appointed for Judah: a time of judgment
alternatives: a harvest of blessing for Judah
decisions.reason: Harvest is a common picture of judgment, when the crop is cut down (Jeremiah 51:33; Joel 4:13). Judah has been named alongside Ephraim in guilt (5:10-14; 6:4), so it too has a harvest coming. The verb has no stated subject ("he has appointed"); it is the LORD who sets the time. Some take the harvest as a promise of good, tied to the restoring of fortunes that follows.

decisions.choice: when I would restore the fortunes of my people: the start of a sentence that runs into 7:1
alternatives: a harvest is set for you, when I restore the fortunes of my people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew's main division falls before these words, and the next verse begins in the same way: "when I would heal Israel". Read together, the two lines say that whenever the LORD sets out to restore and heal his people, their guilt comes into the open and stands in the way. The words can also be read with the first half of this verse: "a harvest is set for you, when I restore the fortunes of my people". The verse division does not settle it.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes: turn the people's ruin back into good
decisions.reason: The phrase means to reverse a disaster and bring back good days, often after exile (Deuteronomy 30:3; Jeremiah 30:3; Amos 9:14).

decisions.choice: When I would restore the fortunes (L, B); Whenever I want to make things good again (R); comma at the end
decisions.reason: "Restore the fortunes" is the settled wording, and Readable says "make things good again", as in Jeremiah. "Would" and "whenever" give the sense of the Hebrew verb here, of something the LORD sets out to do. The sentence runs on into 7:1, so the verse ends with a comma (m2).

decisions.choice: "restaurar la suerte" (L, B); "hacer que todo vuelva a ir bien" (R)
decisions.reason: Restore the fortunes as the Spanish prophets and Psalms have it (Jeremiah note). The sentence runs on into 7:1, so it ends with a comma, as the English.

decisions.choice: "운명을 돌이키다" (L), "형편을 회복시키다" (B), "다시 잘되게 해 주다" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording settled for "restore the fortunes" in the prophets. The clause is left open, as in the English, because the sentence runs on into 7:1.

decisions.choice: "rétablir le sort" (L, B), "rendre ... de nouveau heureux" (R); a deity_pronoun span on "mon peuple", where the English has none
decisions.reason: The phrase as the term sheet carries it over from Jeremiah; God's own possessive takes the span here as everywhere else in Hosea.
